LESSON: PERCUSSION MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.5: Percussion Musical Instruments
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Percussion Musical Instruments, part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How are percussion musical instruments played?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify percussion musical instruments from diverse Kenyan communities,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Percussion Musical Instruments in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. improvise percussion musical instrument using locally available materials,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Percussion Musical Instruments in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. play a percussion musical instrument for enjoyment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Percussion Musical Instruments in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate percussion musical instruments from diverse Kenyan cultural communities. ● Learners to search for percussion instruments from print and electronic media and identify them. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be supported. ● Learners to visit actual or virtual sites to watch or observe and identify percussion instruments. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with health conditions. Ensure cybersecurity as learners visits virtual sites. ● Learners to collect appropriate locally available materials to How are percussion musical instruments played? 34 improvise shakers or jingles. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with health conditions. ● Learners to play varied rhythms using shakers, jingles or drums to different body movements. Create a safe conducive environment. ● Learners to play percussion musical instrument to accompany a singing games. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, or mime the song. Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body, perform an alternative corresponding activity, or perform at their level of functional ability. ● Learners to positively critique improvised percussion musical instruments, and store them for future reference. 35

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Percussion Musical Instruments together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: as the learner exhibits teamwork as they play jingles and shakers to accompany a

singing game performance for enjoyment

• Creativity and imagination: as the learner undertakes tasks that require skills to improvise shakers and jingles using locally

available materials.

• Digital literacy: as the learner identifies percussion instruments from digital sites.

Values:
• Responsibility: is promoted as the learner clears the working areas after improvising shakers and jingles using locally

available materials and stores them.

• Unity: is nurtured as the learner collaborates and works harmoniously with others.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental conservation: is promoted as the learner responsibly uses locally available materials to improvise

percussion instruments.

• Patriotism: The learner identifies, improvises and plays instruments from Kenyan communities for cultural expression.

Link to other learning areas:

Indigenous language activities: as the learners identify percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Open space, reusable locally available material for making improvised shakers and jingles, resource persons, visual recordings

of musical instrument(shakers and jingles), flash cards, digital devices, musical instruments, assistive technology such as

universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, digital devices, adapted digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head

control input devices such as head wand
